title: OpenModel Bridge: conversion, version-pin flow, and canonical benchmarking
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Implement the 'OpenModel Bridge' pipeline: a guarded, auditable flow that ingests community weights (HF/git-lfs/etc.), verifies provenance and signatures, converts artifacts into Redwood runtime artifacts, pins a semver-compatible model release, and publishes a canonical performance profile to the model catalog. This ticket covers the end-to-end automation and gate rules required to safely onboard new open-source LLMs for hosted and dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Weights intake accepts urls and HF model IDs and stores raw artifacts with provenance metadata (uploader, commit hash, source archive when available).
Automated authenticity checks run: checksum verification, optional signature verification, and a first-pass license classifier with human-review flagging.
Conversion step produces runtime-ready artifacts (quantization optional) and emits an immutable artifact ID; conversion logs saved for auditing.

Performance profile runner executes standardized microbenchmarks (latency p50/p95, throughput, memory, and token cost estimates) at 3 sequence-lengths and publishes a canonical profile to the model catalog.

Model versioning is created following semver-like rules: major.minor.patch + build metadata (source-id). The published model entry is pin-able by customers and supports automatic fallback mapping to compatible variants.
A gating policy enforces: security_review_required OR manual_approve for models with flagged licenses, failing tests, or unusual kernel compatibility.
End-to-end test harness (unit + integration) included, and CI passes for a sample set of 3 community models (small, medium, large).
Changes include docs: onboarding runbook (confluence link), catalog schema changes, and a migration plan for existing unpublished artifacts.
implementation_notes: Pipeline composed of 4 stages: intake -> authenticity -> conversion -> benchmarking/publish. Use isolated ephemeral conversion workers with network egress controls for untrusted artifacts. Store provenance in artifact metadata (source_url, git_sha, signed_by, ingest_user). Conversion toolchain should emit deterministic hashes and include a reproducible-build flag. Benchmark runner uses existing perf harness but adds cost-model estimation and per-token microprofiling.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: malicious or mis-licensed weights accepted into catalog. Mitigation: default quarantine, automated license classifier, and mandatory security review for non-standard licenses. Risk: conversion-induced regressions vs upstream model. Mitigation: run evasion/diff-quality checks using a small standardized eval set and compare to baseline if available.
rollout_plan: Alpha: enable pipeline for internal eng team models only; monitor errors and audit logs (1 week).
Beta: open to selected community models with manual approvals and slack alerts to model-onboarding channel (2 weeks).
GA: full automation with policy gates and catalog publishing; enable customer pinning via API.
test_plan: Unit tests for signature/licensing classifier and deterministic conversion outputs.
Integration tests that run the full pipeline end-to-end on 3 sample HF models (tested nightly).
Performance regression check against previous runtime-1.18 baselines for identical conversion flags.
Chaos test: simulate slow network and partial artifact corruption during intake to validate rollback/quarantine.
